Alright, I just made a targeted edit to the regex in `agent.ts` under the Glint CLI source tree. The change expands the set of heuristic phrases the agent uses when trying to infer the content of a file. That tweak is important for improving the assistant’s ability to guess file contents without explicit prompts.

Now that the source has been modified, the next logical step is to rebuild the CLI so the updated logic is reflected in the executable that users run. I need to make sure the TypeScript code still type‑checks before attempting a build—any type errors would cause the build to fail or produce a broken binary. The project uses Bun, so the appropriate command is `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`. Running it with `--noEmit` ensures it only checks types without generating output, which is fast and safe.

Assuming the type check passes, I should compile the TypeScript entry point (`src/index.tsx`) into a native binary. The repository’s build script uses `bun build` with the `--compile` flag to produce a single executable. I’ll direct the output to `dist/glint`. I only need the final line of the build output to see if any errors slipped through, so piping to `tail -1` will give me a concise status.

Before swapping in the new binary, I must make sure no lingering Glint processes are holding onto the old executable. The test harness runs Glint inside a tmux session named `glint`, so I should terminate that session (`tmux kill-session -t glint`). A short pause (`sleep 0.8`) gives the session time to shut down cleanly. Additionally, there might be a background Glint process still running (perhaps launched directly from `~/.local/bin/glint`), so I’ll use `fuser -k ~/.local/bin/glint` to kill any such process, followed by another brief `sleep` to ensure the OS releases the file handle.

With the old process stopped, I can safely copy the freshly built binary from `dist/glint` into the user’s local bin directory (`~/.local/bin/glint`). To confirm the operation succeeded, I’ll echo a sentinel string `FINAL-INSTALL-OK`. Finally, I’ll run `glint --version` to verify that the installed CLI is functional and reports the expected version, which also serves as a quick sanity check that the binary is executable.

Putting all these steps together into a single Bash command keeps the workflow atomic and ensures that each sub‑step only proceeds if the previous one succeeded (thanks to the `&&` chaining). This will give me a clean build, install, and verification cycle right after the source edit.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is a Bash command that:
1. Type‑checks with `bunx tsc`.
2. Builds the binary with `bun build`.
3. Shows the last line of build output.
4. Kills the tmux session and any running Glint process.
5. Copies the new binary into `~/.local/bin`.
6. Echoes a confirmation marker.
7. Prints the installed version.

Executing this will finalize the changes I just made and let me test the updated behavior immediately.
